key_insight: In a small randomized placebo-controlled trial, an oral polypore fungi combination (FoTv) appeared safe and showed early signals of symptom reduction in mild-to-moderate COVID-19.
clinical_relevance: This early-phase study suggests a low-cost, at-home adjunct worth further testing, but it is not enough to support routine clinical use.
method: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase I trial (26 FoTv, 24 placebo)
Non-hospitalized adults with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 enrolled within 96 hours of diagnosis and 9 days of symptom onset
Safety labs, adherence, symptom scores, CRP, and in vitro pseudovirus infection were assessed
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high adherence, low dropout, normal safety labs overall, and exploratory reductions in symptom burden and C-reactive protein, plus reduced pseudovirus cellular infection in vitro.
watch_item: Findings are preliminary, sample size is small, and symptom benefits and antiviral effects need confirmation in larger trials before implementation.
paper_title: Safety, Feasibility, and Preliminary Clinical Findings of an Oral Polypore Fungi Combination with Mild-to-Moderate COVID-19: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Phase I Clinical Trial
